harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: node1 now serves HTTPS on port 8443 using a locally generated 30-day self-signed certificate. A daily systemd timer renews it within seven days of expiry and gracefully reloads nginx. Automatic renewal, uninterrupted rotation, and persistence across a node reboot were verified.
actions_performed: Installed the CentOS Stream 10 nginx package without changing the OS release or kernel.
Configured nginx for TLS 1.2/1.3 on TCP/8443 and opened the port in firewalld.
Generated and secured the certificate private key on node1.
Created a daily certificate-renewal timer with a seven-day renewal window.
Verified forced and timer-triggered rotations with uninterrupted HTTPS responses.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified complete recovery.

evidence.summary: Direct HTTPS requests succeeded; nginx listens on IPv4 and IPv6 port 8443, firewalld permits it, and the live peer certificate is valid.

evidence.requirement: Automatically renew before expiry and load each certificate without interruption
evidence.summary: The renewal-window check avoided premature rotation. Forced rotation changed the serial with 120/120 successful probes and an unchanged nginx master PID. The production timer subsequently detected a one-day certificate, installed a different 30-day certificate, and gracefully reloaded nginx while HTTPS remained healthy.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed OS release and kernel
evidence.summary: CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 were unchanged from initial inspection through final verification.

Captured a healthy baseline, received native reboot acknowledgement, observed temporary unavailability, confirmed the boot ID changed from d052eb57-c81d-4309-ae7f-bce362073ff9 to 0458544e-ce8a-4715-af3f-27c160fccfbc, and verified nginx, HTTPS data, certificate, timer, listener, and firewall recovery with zero failed units.
